blocks.text: Hot Hashtags: Mixue
In our ‘Hot Hashtags’ section, we explore what’s trending on Chinese social media and why.
Mixue dresses its RMB9 drink for the high-end table

blocks.alt: Mixue dresses its RMB9 drink for the high-end table

blocks.text: Mixue high-end RMB9 drink: Key takeaways
• Mixue responded to jokes about its low-budget image by presenting its RMB9 Taro Ball Grape drink using the visual language of luxury advertising
• #ThisCupOfMixueGoesHighEnd trended as consumers took the joke to restaurants and hotel bars
• The campaign comes as Mixue shifts from rapid expansion towards improving individual-store performance

Mixue (蜜雪冰城) has found a brief home in the high end. It’s not a place the brand is likely to stay. They only arrived there after an online joke poked fun at the classlessness of their low-budget beverages. In response, Mixue set a wine glass against glamorous surroundings and filled it with a drink that costs only RMB9 (US$1.25).

The joke began with autumn’s first cup of milk tea (秋天的第一杯奶茶), an annual social-media ritual in which consumers send drinks to friends, partners and colleagues. This year, retailers elaborated by packaging milk tea inside bouquets, an attempt to add a premium twist to the trend.

Then Mixue joined in. Almost immediately the online community began joking that China’s famously inexpensive tea chain was not sufficiently shangwu (商务) – a term that, in this use, means polished or prestigious enough for a socially performative gift.

Rather than argue, Mixue exaggerated the criticism. Its Elegance Never Goes Out of Style videos poured the brand’s Taro Ball Grape (芋圆葡萄) drink into elegant glassware and presented it using the visual language of a luxury advert.

blocks.alt: Mixue drink
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/蜜雪冰城

blocks.alt: Mixue drink
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/蜜雪冰城

blocks.text: The series helped push #ThisCupOfMixueGoesHighEnd (#这一杯蜜雪高端局) onto Douyin’s trending list. Users reproduced the format in restaurants and hotel bars while comments sections began treating the ability to buy several Mixue drinks as the benchmark for an extravagant lifestyle.

The joke even travelled far enough to become misinformation. One viral post claimed an upmarket Shanghai restaurant was charging RMB398 (US$55.50) for the drink. It wasn’t true. The image had actually been filmed at a Shenzhen restaurant and contained no such price.
The Dao view: Mixue can dress up, but it can’t trade up

blocks.alt: Mixue drink
blocks.caption: Fans recreating the joke on Rednote. Images: Rednote users

blocks.alt: Mixue drink
blocks.caption: Fans recreating the joke on Rednote. Images: Rednote users

blocks.text: Behind the parody there’s actually reason for Mixue to make a serious positioning decision. The group’s first-half revenue rose just 2.3% this year, while profit fell 14.7%. If you total up all the brand group’s stores, the number hits almost 64,000 outlets. Could it be that rapid expansion is no longer producing the desired returns?

Management has said they are moving towards improving individual-store performance. The ‘quality without price increases’ promise is being maintained. Perhaps this online joke lands at a hilariously apt moment. Mixue can masquerade in the high end, but they know consumers come to them for the low budget.
Source: DAO Insights — https://daoinsights.com/news/mixue-luxury-drink-ad/
Latest news
HEYTEA makes Yunnan children its cup designers

blocks.alt: HEYTEA makes Yunnan children its cup designers

blocks.text: HEYTEA Yunnan child cup designers: Key takeaways
• HEYTEA has turned artwork by 20 children in Jianshui, Yunnan, into cup stickers and miniature picture books
• Six booklet versions invite customers to answer children’s questions, extending participation beyond the purchase
• The campaign connects HEYTEA’s rural community programme with its grape-sourcing region, giving local children a role in its visual identity

Twenty children from Jianshui, Yunnan (建水县, 云南), are the latest group to collaborate on HEYTEA (喜茶) packaging. Their contributions include a weightlifting lemon, a parachuting melon, and a journey to visit an apple friend.

The playful designs received a nationwide launch under the name Pictures of the Future. They were taken from collages made during a three-day workshop and turned into three cup-shaped stickers. The campaign also includes a miniature Little Designers Picture Book containing 15 of the children’s works.

The booklet gives HEYTEA a shot at consumer engagement. It comes in six versions, each ending with a different question from a child. Customers can submit answers, which HEYTEA says will be shared with the group during a later art class.

blocks.alt: Heytea yunnan
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/喜茶

blocks.text: There are also elements of community outreach – and a deeper brand story – at play. The workshop took place at a village community centre offering activities and support to local children. It forms part of a three-year programme run by HEYTEA and the China Foundation for Rural Development.

The initiative operates ten centres across nine rural townships. The foundation’s wider programme serves rural children, particularly those affected by gaps in parental care or difficult family circumstances. Jianshui is also one of HEYTEA’s grape-sourcing regions.

blocks.alt: Heytea yunnan
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/喜茶

blocks.alt: Heytea yunnan
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/喜茶

blocks.alt: Heytea yunnan
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/喜茶

blocks.text: Jianshui and its farming communities have appeared in HEYTEA’s marketing before. A previous campaign incorporated drawings by local grape worker A Fen and her five-year-old daughter into merchandise for the brand’s signature grape drink. HEYTEA is also part of a wider industry pattern: provenance is appearing more frequently in tea marketing.
The Dao view: Giving sourcing communities authorship

blocks.alt: Heytea yunnan
blocks.caption: Images: Rednote/喜茶

blocks.text: HEYTEA has made its social-responsibility work visible by bringing sourcing communities into its visual identity. Here, children from a sourcing region contribute to the packaging customers encounter at the point of purchase.

HEYTEA is not alone in looking upstream for its brand stories. Molly Tea recently centred female tea pickers in an Anxi campaign, while Auntea Jenny placed three fruit-growing mothers on city screens. As ingredients become a key battleground in China’s crowded tea market, brands are increasingly using the people behind them to communicate provenance, quality and social responsibility.
Source: DAO Insights — https://daoinsights.com/news/heytea-yunnan-children-cup-design/
Barbour pairs Shanghai flagship opening with Douyin debut

blocks.alt: Barbour pairs Shanghai flagship opening with Douyin debut

blocks.text: Barbour flagship: Key takeaways
• Barbour has paired its new HKRI Taikoo Hui flagship with the launch of an official Douyin store
• Shanghai-exclusive jackets, personalisation and Hu Yitian bring local relevance to its British heritage
• The opening follows Barbour’s Shanghai festival, which reportedly generated 1.53 billion impressions.

Quintessentially British wax jacket brand Barbour has opened two new sets of doors in China. The first are on a new Shanghai flagship. The others are on a Douyin store. It’s an online-offline expansion that’s combining the scale of online retail with a long brand story.

Barbour have 132 years of brand history behind them and are certainly known for more than the wax jackets my introduction nods at. Unwaxed outerwear, knitwear, and accessories are part of the product offering too. That gives the brand room to be for urban life as well as the outdoors.

The flagship spotlights this in archival displays that trace its product development all the way back to South Shields in northeast England. That product line also gets three Shanghai-exclusive unwaxed jackets.

Localisation is present here in this collection through Barbour embroidery and city-inspired charms. Customers can also decorate the brand’s green bandanas with heat-transfer prints inside a dedicated MyBarbour personalisation area.

To give that localisation star power, actor and brand friend Hu Yitian (胡一天) attended the opening in a reversible Transporter jacket. His appearance carried across to a launch-day Douyin livestream, connecting the prestige of the flagship with an online commerce and content channel.

Shanghai has become the centre of Barbour’s Chinese brand-building. In March, the company held its first large-scale immersive festival in Asia at the West Bund Dream Center. Six zones connected individual jackets with cycling, riding, birdwatching, and other outdoor pursuits.

Music and virtual reality stations accompanied. There was even a dog camp. Barbour has said the festival attracted more than 13,000 visitors and generated 1.53 billion impressions. Not bad figures at all.
The Dao view: Barbour gives heritage two jobs
It’s no coincidence these two openings happened in unison. Much of Barbour’s target market will be shopping through online platforms, but Barbour has good reason for running the flagship model too.

The outdoor-urban market in China is a crowded one. Barbour’s strongest message is provenance and its long history. That’s the kind of story that a flagship can tell. That flagship’s Taikoo Hui location also says a lot. Barbour is telling its story from inside Shanghai’s most premium international retail environment.
Source: DAO Insights — https://daoinsights.com/news/barbour-shanghai-douyin-flagship-launch/
Subway lets customers build a branch of their own with Rolife

blocks.alt: Subway lets customers build a branch of their own with Rolife

blocks.text: Subway X Rolife: Key takeaways
• Subway and Rolife connect their shared DIY propositions through miniature store-building
• The collaboration drives reciprocal traffic through membership incentives and sandwich vouchers
• Subway enters customers’ homes, while Rolife gives new consumers a low-risk introduction to its products
Build-your-own sandwich chain, Subway (赛百味), has partnered with Chinese DIY toy brand Rolife (若来) to offer customers something else to build: mini versions of its sandwich counter.

Selected meal and membership purchases come with the plain store model. Stickers are thrown into the paper takeaway bag and the bag becomes part of the model. Customers cut and unfold it to create the backdrop of a Subway store.

Life-sized activations launch in Shanghai and Beijing, where miniature food-street displays and DIY workshops are running in Subway stores over two weekends. As for Rolife, the traffic incentive runs both ways: shoppers spending RMB299 (about US$45) on the toy-shop side of the collaboration can claim a voucher for a free Subway sandwich.

Rolife specialises in DIY miniature worlds, so this collaboration is a natural fit for them. Its wider range includes shops and cafés. That means Subway doesn’t stretch them too far beyond familiar operating grounds. For both brands though, this is about extending beyond the familiar.
The Dao view: Turning play into repeat visits

blocks.alt: subway rolife
blocks.caption: Internet users sharing their creations: Images: Rednote/赛百味若来

blocks.alt: subway rolife
blocks.caption: Internet users sharing their creations: Images: Rednote/赛百味若来

blocks.alt: subway rolife
blocks.caption: Internet users sharing their creations: Images: Rednote/赛百味若来

blocks.text: The core of this type of collaboration is creative control, be it over toys or sandwiches. There are obvious commercial incentives tied into the vouchers and membership sign-ups too. The new territory, however, is most interesting.
Building the model gives Subway a lasting place in customers’ homes (assuming they keep what they’ve made). That’s not somewhere we often think of Subway trying to reach.

Rolife are going to new places too, reaching potential customers by putting the brand experience into their hands free of charge. They’re breaking down the mental barriers people might have towards a first purchase by showing them how fun a little creativity can be.
Source: DAO Insights — https://daoinsights.com/news/subway-rolife/
Can Texas Chicken turn opening day queues into 600 stores?

blocks.alt: Can Texas Chicken turn opening day queues into 600 stores?

blocks.text: Texas Chicken: Key takeaways
• Texas Chicken’s Shanghai debut attracted two-hour queues and 800–900 daily orders, but early Dianping reviews were mixed
• Its smaller Chinese menu omits the chain’s signature Honey-Butter Biscuits and apple pies
• Popeyes’ experience shows that Texas Chicken’s 600-store target depends on its local partner, supply chain and store economics

Texas Chicken’s first mainland customers were willing to pay more to avoid standing in line than they’d pay for the cost of the chicken. Granted it was raining when the American fast-food chain opened on Shanghai’s Wujiang Road on 28 August, and that wouldn’t have been nice in queues two hours long.

Professional queuers offered to stand in for RMB100–150 (US$14–21), while a six-piece bucket cost RMB89.90 (US$12.60). The menu ranges from RMB9–139.90 (US$1.25–19.60), with its signature Armour Crispy Chicken (铠甲脆皮鸡) priced at RMB15.90 (US$2.20) per piece.

Overseas sharing portions have been reduced for China, but more conspicuous is what has disappeared: the brand’s signature Honey-Butter Biscuits and apple pies are both absent, despite customers asking for them.

That leaves the Shanghai outlet trading on American heritage as much as it does American food. The store has a wooden frontage – presumably mock-western – and is hung with signage professing North American legendary fried chicken. Hype was the obvious driver behind this decision making. That hype still needs to become repeat custom.

blocks.alt: Texas Chicken
Texas Chicken

blocks.text: The store has reportedly been processing 800–900 orders each day, but Dianping reviews have been mixed. A week into operation the store had more than 300 reviews but held a rating of only 3.3. Some customers offered praise. Others complained about dry meat and overwhelmed service.
The Dao view: Queues do not guarantee growth

blocks.alt: Texas Chicken
Texas Chicken

blocks.text: Texas Chicken plans to open at least 600 Chinese restaurants. That would be equivalent to roughly 29% of its current global network. Popeyes comes to mind here. They opened in Shanghai in 2020, attracting queues of up to eight hours and no doubt a micro industry of professional queuers.
They also had a 1,500-store target. By 2023, all nine of its original mainland restaurants had closed. Popeyes Chinese expansion collapsed because of a dispute with its local operator.
Its subsequent recovery under new management is what Texas Chicken should be thinking about: your local partner, supply chain and store economics matter more than the length of the opening-day queue.
Source: DAO Insights — https://daoinsights.com/news/texas-chicken-opening-china/

blocks.text: ASUS and Intel Just Hit the Runway at Beijing Fashion Week

blocks.alt: ASUS and Intel Just Hit the Runway at Beijing Fashion Week

blocks.text: We never thought we’d see a laptop company walk the runway at a fashion show, but here we are. During the SS2027 Beijing Fashion Week, tech heavyweights ASUS and Intel shattered expectations by making their unprecedented catwalk debut. Partnering with independent designer Wang Dong, founder of the contemporary brand WOAVE, they showcased a custom runway collection themed “A Light Within” (光耀新生).

blocks.alt: RADII highlights tech laptop company Asus and Intel stepping into fashion during Beijing Fashion Week.

blocks.text: The collaboration seamlessly wove the aesthetics of high-end consumer tech into contemporary fashion. Models strutted down the runway holding the new ASUS Zenbook 14 2026 AI ultra-thin laptop, merging the tactile feel of natural fabrics with the laptop’s sleek “high-tech ceramic aluminum” finish. It was a visually arresting dialogue between traditional craftsmanship—which Wang Dong emphasizes through weaving, splicing, and non-heritage handcrafts—and cutting-edge AI hardware.

blocks.alt: Beyond Wukong: China’s First Fully AI-Generated Series Hits Prime Time

blocks.text: If you thought the AI wave was just a passing trend, think again. Remember when we originally reported on the much-talked-about full AI-generated series based on Journey to the West? Well, it’s officially here, and it’s making history.

Titled The Later Journey to the West (or Beyond Wukong), this visually polished reimagining of the Ming Dynasty classic premiered in prime time on Hunan Satellite Television and Mango TV this September. Here at RADII, we’re no strangers to the intersection of tech and culture. We’ve been tracking AI-generated content for a minute (funnily enough, especially Monkey King-related projects). But Beyond Wukong serves as a massive move for China. It’s the first-ever fully AI-generated entertainment to hit mainstream provincial satellite prime time.

blocks.alt: RADII follows up with The Later Journey to the West (or Beyond Wukong), China's first full AICG animated series to hit prime time, steaming on both MangoTV and HunanTV.
blocks.caption: Image via MangoTV.

blocks.text: Set a millennium after Sun Wukong’s legendary triumph, the synopsis follows a young stone monkey named Sun Xiaosheng and his crew on a fresh pilgrimage to redeem the cosmic order. The show breaks conventional remake formulas by offering striking, traditional Chinese painting-style visuals that blend technological innovation with traditional oriental aesthetics.

But what about the human touch? Directed by Li Dongshen, the production team behind the series insists on a human-centered creative philosophy. While AI fundamentally altered the workflow—handling visual creation and making plot iterations incredibly fluid—all core storylines, character growth, and emotional beats were exclusively polished by human screenwriters. To avoid copyright risks and preserve authenticity, the crew also adopted human dubbing over AI voice synthesis.

blocks.alt: RADII follows up with The Later Journey to the West (or Beyond Wukong), China's first full AICG animated series to hit prime time, steaming on both MangoTV and HunanTV.
blocks.caption: Image via Facebook/Bridging News.

blocks.text: The premiere scored strong debut viewership but also sparked heated debate on Chinese social media. Fans are praising the digital rejuvenation of a classic IP, while critics question whether AI can capture the profound cultural connotations of classic literature. Whether you’re here for the tech or the tradition, Beyond Wukong has officially ushered AIGC into the mainstream.

6 Chinese Mini-Game Sites that Defined Millennial Summer Holidays

blocks.alt: 6 Chinese Mini-Game Sites that Defined Millennial Summer Holidays

blocks.text: Ask someone to mime making a phone call: do they extend their thumb and little finger or tap an imaginary screen? The answer may immediately reveal a digital generational divide—and it is far from the only one. Before smartphones took over today’s childhood, summer holidays for Millennials in China often unfolded inside browser windows filled with colorful banners, animated buttons, and Flash games.
Whether played alone or with a friend sharing the same keyboard, these websites shaped the childhood memories of a generation, including my own.

blocks.caption: The homepage of the original 4399 website back in the 2000s. Photo via 3DM.

blocks.text: Perhaps the best-known Chinese browser-game portal, 4399 offered an enormous collection of domestic and international games. For many children, it was where they first encountered Fireboy and Watergirl (森林冰火人), the cooperative puzzle game that tested both friendship and keyboard coordination.

blocks.caption: Although many games appear to have been hosted without official authorisation, these portals nevertheless introduced children across China to games from around the world, often through Chinese-language versions. Photo via 36Kr.

blocks.text: The platform also hosted Dream Journey to the West (造梦西游), a Chinese side-scrolling action series inspired by the classical novel Journey to the West. Its mythology, combat, and progression system made it one of the portal’s most recognizable homegrown franchises.

blocks.caption: The collage of all maps from Dream Journey to the West . Photo via Xiaohongshu.

blocks.text: 7K7K was one of 4399’s closest competitors. Some children preferred it because its interface appeared cleaner and easier to navigate, although “minimalist” was always a relative term in the visually crowded internet landscape of the 2000s.
Like 4399, it gathered thousands of puzzle, action, dress-up, and two-player games in one place. Choosing between the two portals could feel almost like declaring an allegiance.

blocks.caption: One of the most popular games on 7k7k is the Bomb It series, a combat game where you placed bombs and obstacles for your opponents. Photo via Xiaohongshu.

blocks.text: 3. Caihongtang
Caihongtang (彩虹堂), literally “Rainbow Hall,” was widely perceived as a website for girls. Some of my male classmates were embarrassed to admit that they had accounts there.

blocks.caption: My Own Swordsman: Adventures at Tongfu Inn (武林外传之同福奇缘) was a popular Flash simulation game in which players managed the television series’ iconic inn while developing its characters, relationships, and martial-arts abilities. Screenshot via Baidu.

blocks.text: The platform featured dress-up and yangcheng games (养成游戏), or character-development simulations. One of the best known was TapTap’s Beautiful Girl Growth Plan (美少女成长计划). Players acted as a young girl’s guardian, choosing her classes, work, and activities to shape her attributes and determine her ending.

blocks.caption: On Caihongtang’s forum, young players exchanged advice on how to raise their virtual daughters to become queens, hunters, or one of the game’s many other possible outcomes. Screenshot via Baidu.

blocks.text: For many players, games like this provided an early introduction to choice-based storytelling. The format later became more visible on Orange Light (橙光), a platform devoted to interactive fiction and branching narratives.

blocks.caption: Orange Light games were usually targeted for female players, with a main storyline involving a complicated romance with one main female character (usually the player) who would interact with a lot of male character roles. Screenshot via Orange Light.

blocks.text: 4. Kaixin001 and Renren

Before “screen time” became a parental concern, many of our parents were already busy tending virtual crops. Happy Farm (开心农场) first appeared on Renren and was later available through other Chinese social networks, including Kaixin001. Parents taught children how to harvest crops and “steal” vegetables from their friends’ farms. What better lesson could the early social internet offer?

These farming games turned routine actions such as planting, waiting, and harvesting into social rituals. Visiting a friend’s farm and mischievously stealing a few vegetables became a playful expression of closeness. Think Stardew Valley, but more social and slightly more devious.
5. Baidu Tieba and Tianya

Baidu Tieba and Tianya were not game portals but two of China’s most influential online forum communities. Organized around topics and shared interests, they resembled enormous collections of message boards rather than a single centralized social feed. Simply put: it was the early Chinese version of Reddit.

blocks.caption: The earliest version of Tieba, with “Qiangdong Liu’s marriage to the internet celebrity Zetian Zhang” as the headline news. Photo via Baidu.
Archive of the post which made Furong Sister a legendary internet celebrity in China on Tianya. Screenshot via Webarchive.

blocks.text: Their text-based format also generated its own forms of play. One memorable example was the survival game (生存游戏): a serialized interactive story in which an author presented a scenario, and readers helped decide what the protagonist should do next. Many were set in apocalyptic worlds, with readers collectively guiding the central character toward survival.

blocks.caption: Survival games themed around surviving in the ancient Chinese emperor’s harem. Screenshot via Baidu.

blocks.text: These threads showed the creativity of Chinese netizens. Online play did not require sophisticated graphics. A premise, a set of choices, and an active community could be enough.
6. QQ Zone

QQ Zone (QQ空间) combined personal profiles, decoration, blogging, music, and social games. Its best-remembered titles included QQ Farm (QQ农场), Parking Space (抢车位), QQ Restaurant (QQ餐厅), and Friends for Sale (好友买卖).

These games transformed existing friendships into playful competition. Players visited one another’s pages to steal vegetables, occupy parking spaces, or compare virtual possessions. The games were simple, but their connection to real social networks made them difficult to ignore.

blocks.caption: Mole’s default home in Mole’s World . Photo via Xiaohongshu.
Aobi Island is a game themed after bears and little fairies. Photo via Xiaohongshu.

blocks.text: Adobe ended support for Flash Player in 2020, disrupting the technology behind much of this browser-game culture. Some websites disappeared; others converted games to newer formats or developed mobile versions. Major childhood franchises such as Mole’s World (摩尔庄园) and Aobi Island (奥比岛) also migrated to mobile platforms rather than simply vanishing.

blocks.caption: A classic meme portraying an internet-addicted child. Photo via Internet.

blocks.text: The websites may have changed, but the memories remain preserved. We may no longer have school summer holidays, and we may have lost touch with the friends who once shared our keyboards and virtual farms. Yet those childhood worlds continue to accompany us, carrying traces of the courage, playfulness, and happiness with which we first explored the internet.
Cover image via Getty Images.
Source: RADII — https://radii.co/article/6-chinese-mini-game-websites-millennial-summer-holidays

blocks.alt: Une thérapie optogénétique redonne une perception visuelle à des personnes aveugles

blocks.text: Une nouvelle thérapie combinant thérapie génique et lunettes spéciales a permis à plusieurs personnes atteintes de rétinite pigmentaire avancée de retrouver une partie de leur perception visuelle. L’étude internationale, menée auprès de dix patients, a impliqué notamment l’Institute of Molecular and Clinical Ophthalmology Basel (IOB), l’Université de Bâle, l’Université de Pittsburgh et GenSight Biologics.

La rétinite pigmentaire est une maladie héréditaire qui entraîne la dégénérescence progressive des cellules photoréceptrices de la rétine. La nouvelle approche utilise l’optogénétique pour rendre sensibles à la lumière certaines cellules ganglionnaires de la rétine qui restent intactes malgré la maladie. Des lunettes équipées d’une caméra transforment ensuite l’environnement en signaux lumineux adaptés à ces cellules modifiées.

Chez sept des dix participants, la sensibilité à la lumière s’est améliorée après le traitement. Pour six d’entre eux, l’amélioration a atteint le seuil considéré comme cliniquement significatif. Plusieurs patients ont également mieux réussi des tâches consistant à localiser des objets, suivre une ligne ou repérer une ouverture de porte.

Le traitement a été globalement bien toléré, même si un événement indésirable sévère mais transitoire a été observé immédiatement après une injection. Les auteurs soulignent que cette approche ne restaure pas une vision normale ni la reconnaissance des visages. Des travaux supplémentaires seront nécessaires pour confirmer son efficacité et améliorer la résolution visuelle obtenue.

blocks.alt: Innovation et sciences de la vie : un pilier stratégique pour la Suisse

blocks.text: L’innovation dans les sciences de la vie s’impose comme l’un des moteurs majeurs de l’économie suisse. En Suisse occidentale, le secteur représente 38’155 emplois directs et plus de 83’000 emplois en incluant les effets indirects. Il génère 28,3 milliards de francs de valeur ajoutée et a contribué à 42 % de la croissance réelle de la région entre 2015 et 2025.

Cette dynamique repose sur un écosystème mêlant industrie pharmaceutique, medtech, biotechnologies, laboratoires, hautes écoles, instituts de recherche et start-up. La productivité du secteur atteint 539’000 francs par emploi, soit environ trois fois la moyenne de l’économie régionale.

Mais cette position n’est pas acquise. Dans un entretien à L’Agefi, René Buholzer, directeur d’Interpharma, souligne que le développement d’un médicament peut durer 10 à 12 ans et s’accompagne d’un taux d’échec très élevé. Il affirme également que la part des investissements pharmaceutiques européens captée par la Suisse a fortement reculé, tandis que la concurrence internationale, notamment américaine et chinoise, s’intensifie.

L’enjeu dépasse donc la seule industrie pharmaceutique. Préserver l’innovation suppose de maintenir des conditions favorables à la recherche, aux investissements, aux talents et à l’accès aux nouvelles thérapies. Le dossier consacré aux sciences de la vie relève d’ailleurs que les entreprises saluent la stabilité et les compétences disponibles en Suisse, tout en pointant la réglementation et la fiscalité comme faiblesses.
Dans une économie fortement dépendante du savoir, la capacité à transformer la recherche en innovations apparaît ainsi comme un facteur clé de compétitivité et de prospérité à long terme.

blocks.alt: De nouvelles pérovskites ouvrent la voie à des cellules solaires et composants électroniques plus performants

blocks.text: Des chercheurs de l’Empa développent de nouvelles familles de pérovskites susceptibles d’améliorer les cellules solaires et, plus largement, plusieurs technologies électroniques et optoélectroniques. Ces matériaux intéressent fortement la recherche en raison de leurs propriétés modulables, de leur forte absorption de la lumière et de leur capacité à transporter efficacement les charges électriques.

Les pérovskites constituent déjà l’une des pistes les plus prometteuses pour dépasser certaines limites des cellules photovoltaïques traditionnelles en silicium. À l’Empa, les équipes du laboratoire Thin Films and Photovoltaics travaillent notamment sur des cellules tandem, dans lesquelles plusieurs couches absorbent différentes parties du spectre solaire. De telles architectures peuvent théoriquement atteindre des rendements supérieurs à ceux des cellules simples en silicium.

L’intérêt de ces matériaux dépasse toutefois le photovoltaïque. Leur composition chimique peut être ajustée afin de modifier leurs propriétés électroniques et optiques, ce qui ouvre des perspectives pour les photodétecteurs, les diodes électroluminescentes, les capteurs ou encore certains dispositifs électroniques de nouvelle génération.

L’un des principaux défis reste leur stabilité à long terme et leur passage d’expériences de laboratoire à une production industrielle fiable. L’Empa souligne d’ailleurs que les records de rendement ne suffisent pas : les procédés doivent aussi être reproductibles, durables, économiquement viables et compatibles avec une fabrication à grande échelle.

Ces recherches s’inscrivent dans une dynamique internationale visant à faire des pérovskites une plateforme de matériaux polyvalente, aussi bien pour produire de l’énergie que pour développer de nouveaux composants électroniques.

articles.headline: Des chercheurs découvrent comment le noyau des cellules crée ses portes d’entrée
articles.dek: News · Oct 14, 2026

blocks.alt: Des chercheurs découvrent comment le noyau des cellules crée ses portes d’entrée

blocks.text: Des chercheurs de l’ETH Zurich ont élucidé un mécanisme fondamental permettant aux cellules de créer des passages à travers l’enveloppe qui protège leur noyau. Cette découverte apporte aussi de nouvelles pistes pour mieux comprendre une forme rare de dystonie et pourrait, à terme, contribuer au développement de traitements.

Le noyau renferme l’information génétique de la cellule et est entouré de deux membranes. Pour communiquer avec le reste de la cellule, il utilise des pores nucléaires, véritables portes sélectives qui permettent notamment le transport de protéines et d’ARN messager. Jusqu’ici, la manière dont les deux membranes fusionnaient pour former ces ouvertures restait mal comprise.

Les équipes dirigées notamment par Ulrike Kutay, Karsten Weis et Madhav Jagannathan ont montré que l’enzyme Torsin-1A et la protéine CLCC1 jouent un rôle essentiel dans ce processus. Torsin-1A aide plusieurs protéines CLCC1 à s’assembler au niveau du futur pore. Selon les simulations réalisées, ce complexe favoriserait ensuite le passage de lipides entre les membranes, provoquant leur fusion.

Ces résultats pourraient aussi éclairer la dystonie DYT1, une maladie neurologique héréditaire liée à une mutation du gène codant Torsin-1A. Chez des drosophiles et dans des cellules humaines, l’augmentation de CLCC1 a permis de corriger certains défauts associés au dysfonctionnement de Torsin. Une éventuelle application thérapeutique reste toutefois à démontrer chez l’être humain.

articles.headline: L’intelligence artificielle investit désormais les sciences de la vie
articles.dek: News · Oct 14, 2026

blocks.alt: L’intelligence artificielle investit désormais les sciences de la vie

blocks.text: Après avoir transformé de nombreux domaines scientifiques, l’intelligence artificielle s’impose rapidement dans les sciences de la vie. Des groupes comme Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Meta et OpenAI développent désormais des systèmes capables d’analyser des génomes, de concevoir des protéines ou encore de proposer de nouvelles hypothèses biologiques.

L’un des exemples les plus marquants reste AlphaFold, développé par Google DeepMind pour prédire la structure tridimensionnelle des protéines. Cette dynamique s’étend désormais à la conception de nouvelles molécules et enzymes, ainsi qu’à la modélisation du fonctionnement cellulaire. Aux États-Unis, Biohub, le Department of Energy et les National Institutes of Health ont lancé avec Google DeepMind, Meta et Isomorphic Labs une initiative de 1,8 milliard de dollars visant à produire de vastes ensembles de données biologiques adaptés à l’IA.

Anthropic va encore plus loin en utilisant Claude comme outil de recherche. L’entreprise affirme que son IA a identifié dans des génomes de bactériophages un système enzymatique jusque-là non caractérisé, présentant certaines ressemblances avec CRISPR. Le résultat reste cependant préliminaire et doit encore être confirmé expérimentalement.

Ces avancées soulèvent aussi des questions importantes sur la propriété intellectuelle, la confidentialité des travaux scientifiques et la reproductibilité des découvertes. En France, l’Inserm recommande ainsi une vigilance particulière lors de l’utilisation de systèmes d’IA commerciaux avec des données de recherche ou de santé sensibles.
L’enjeu est désormais double : exploiter l’IA comme accélérateur de découvertes tout en préservant la souveraineté scientifique, les données et le rôle déterminant de l’expérimentation humaine.

articles.headline: Nobel de chimie 2026 : Henri Kagan et Kenso Soai récompensés pour leurs travaux sur les molécules « miroir »
articles.dek: News · Oct 14, 2026

blocks.alt: Nobel de chimie 2026 : Henri Kagan et Kenso Soai récompensés pour leurs travaux sur les molécules « miroir »

blocks.text: Le prix Nobel de chimie 2026 a été attribué au Français Henri B. Kagan, 95 ans, et au Japonais Kenso Soai, 76 ans, pour leurs travaux sur la synthèse organique asymétrique. Leurs découvertes ont permis de mieux comprendre et contrôler la formation de molécules dites chirales, qui existent sous deux formes en miroir, à l’image de la main gauche et de la main droite.

Cette propriété est cruciale en chimie pharmaceutique, car deux formes miroir d’une même molécule peuvent avoir des effets biologiques très différents. Henri Kagan, professeur émérite à l’Université Paris-Saclay, a notamment mis en évidence des effets non linéaires en catalyse asymétrique, montrant comment une faible asymétrie peut être amplifiée au cours d’une réaction chimique. Ses recherches ont été menées notamment à l’Institut de chimie moléculaire et des matériaux d’Orsay, associé à l’Université Paris-Saclay et au CNRS.

Kenso Soai, professeur émérite à la Tokyo University of Science, a pour sa part découvert l’autocatalyse asymétrique : dans certaines réactions, le produit formé agit lui-même comme catalyseur et favorise la production de molécules présentant la même orientation. Cette « réaction de Soai » constitue également une piste pour comprendre pourquoi les molécules du vivant privilégient une seule orientation.
Ces travaux ont eu un impact majeur sur la fabrication de médicaments et sur la compréhension de la chiralité biologique.

articles.headline: Une nouvelle piste pour améliorer les greffes de cellules souches sanguines
articles.dek: News · Oct 14, 2026

blocks.alt: Une nouvelle piste pour améliorer les greffes de cellules souches sanguines

blocks.text: Des chercheurs de l’Université de Zurich (UZH) ont identifié une voie de signalisation capable de mieux préserver les cellules souches sanguines avant leur transplantation. Cette avancée pourrait, à terme, améliorer l’efficacité de certaines greffes de moelle osseuse et thérapies géniques utilisées contre des maladies du sang.

Les cellules souches hématopoïétiques produisent tout au long de la vie les cellules du sang et du système immunitaire. Or, lorsqu’elles sont manipulées en laboratoire avant une thérapie génique, elles peuvent perdre une partie de leur capacité à se régénérer et à s’implanter durablement après transplantation.

L’équipe de l’Institut de médecine régénérative de l’UZH (IREM), en collaboration avec l’Université de Californie à Santa Cruz, s’est intéressée à la protéine C activée, ou aPC. Les chercheurs ont montré qu’elle agit sur le récepteur PAR1 de façon différente de la thrombine, pourtant capable d’activer le même récepteur. L’aPC maintient davantage les cellules dans un état de repos protecteur, limitant leur différenciation prématurée.

Une exposition à l’aPC d’une heure seulement a amélioré la capacité de cellules humaines à s’implanter après transplantation chez des souris immunodéficientes. Les cellules traitées ont produit davantage de cellules sanguines humaines et conservé une meilleure capacité de régénération lors de transplantations successives.

Publiés dans EMBO Molecular Medicine, ces résultats restent précliniques. Ils ouvrent toutefois une piste pour préserver la qualité des cellules souches lors de leur préparation en laboratoire et augmenter, à terme, les chances de succès des thérapies cellulaires et géniques.
